newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan brass demand seen barely higher in 1997/98.
newsitem.headline: Japan brass demand seen barely higher in 1997/98.

text.p: Japan's brass demand is expected to edge up by 0.2 percent in the fiscal year beginning April 1 to 1,193,000 tonnes, after dipping an estimated 1.0 percent in 1996/97, the Japan Brass Makers Association said on Wednesday.

Domestic demand in 1997/98 was forecast to rise 0.5 percent to 992,320 tonnes, compared with a 1.1 percent dip to 987,050 tonnes in 1996/97, while exports were seen falling 1.7 percent in 1997/98 to 200,680 tonnes after dipping 0.6 percent to 204,100 tonnes in 1996/97.

The association said that the scheduled rise in the national sales tax on April 1 was expected to dampen consumer spending and housing construction, although the weak yen would fuel demand from exporting sectors while low interest rates would lend encouragement to the construction industry.
Overall demand from the semiconductor sector, which last October began recovering from a protracted slump, was likely to remain firm in 1997/98, the association said.

Domestic demand for room air conditioners was expected to hold steady at last year's high levels, although production was seen easing slightly in response to bloated inventories, which at the end of January exceeded three million units.
Carmakers were expected to continue switching to aluminium radiators from copper, although this loss would be offset by strong demand for copper in automotive electronics, the association said.
